reaction: The parallel with the earlier insulin response makes the sequence easier to follow.
reason: The glucagon route points toward the liver, which still contains stored glycogen.
expectation: Glucagon should signal the liver to release glucose from its glycogen stores.

reaction: The sequence brought the between-meal response together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Combining the glucagon response with the liver was most worthwhile: the result connected a hormone signal to stored glycogen, glucose release and feedback. The sequential picture description helped explain the relationship.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial attempt was the least worthwhile. It seemed reasonable for pancreatic cells to respond directly to the glucose-rich blood, but the game required the blood to be connected to the body first.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the first combination needed a whole-body intermediate. The compatibility feedback made the required step clear.

arbitrary.text: The required whole-body intermediate felt somewhat arbitrary because the blood sample and pancreatic sensing cells already suggested a direct relationship.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it explored a new relationship with similarly clear cause and effect. This chapter's parallel insulin and glucagon responses were informative, though its mostly predictable sequence offered few meaningful choices.
